## About

Some of the UK's rarest wildlife calls Minsmere nature reserve home. Take an idyllic walk through the reedbed or head to the coastal lagoons to see an array of birds, including Avocets, Bearded Tits and Bitterns. If you're lucky, you might even spot an Otter around the reedbed pools.

Minsmere’s mix of landscapes makes it an ideal spot to see how we manage and protect different habitats for the benefit of wildlife. On a visit to this Suffolk nature reserve, you can look forward to exploring reedbed, shallow lagoons, wet grassland, heathland and vegetated shingle. All our habitats are carefully managed to make them ideal places for thousands of species of wildlife. Take the reedbeds, where Marsh Harrier, Otters and Water Voles can be found. Or the heathlands, where Nightjars churr, Adders slither and Silver-studded Blue Butterflies flutter.

Don't be surprised to see ponies grazing here. They play a vital role improving the habitat for some of our rarest plants and minibeasts, such as the brilliantly named Great Green Bush-cricket. Water is a vital part of Minsmere’s appeal and we work hard to get water and salt levels right across the reserve, as different species thrive in different conditions. We are always developing our ways of managing the land, as well as converting former farmland into acid grassland and heathland, to make more space for birds such as Woodlarks and rare Stone-curlews.

Families can build a den together, explore the trails and play in the Wild Zone’s the newly refurbished play area and the sand martin tunnels. Follow the seasonal self-guided trails in search of Minsmere’s wildlife. Families can take part in family-fun activities, like pond dipping or minibeast hunting, with friendly volunteers, during school holidays.

RSPB Minsmere is a great place to bring the family to enjoy nature on the Suffolk coast. After a friendly welcome in the visitor centre, there’s a choice of easy walks through beautiful woodland, wetland and coastal scenery. After you’ve finished exploring, why not browse our shop for a keepsake or relax and recharge in our nourishing café enjoying picturesque views of Minsmere?

## At a glance

243 spaces.

8 Blue Badge spaces. Blue badge spaces 80 metres from visitor centre via a sloped path.

Drop-off outside visitor centre – beware of vehicles and pedestrians. Level and even pea gravel surface.

2 coach spaces.

No lighting. No height restrictions. No overnight parking or camping. Bicycle racks available.

Please don't park on the road, verges or in gateways, as it causes an obstruction for residents and emergency services.

Our toilets are open dawn to dusk.

Accessible toilet located in visitor centre is open when the visitor centre is.

They are located in our toilets next to our visitor centre.

Some nature trails and hides are adapted for pushchairs. Ask our friendly welcome team for an accessible map on arrival.

There are three mobility scooters available to borrow, booking is essential. To book a mobility scooter please call our Visitor Centre on [01728 648281](tel:01728 648281).

Some nature trails and hides are adapted for wheelchairs.

Our toilets are open dawn to dusk.

They are located in a separate toilet block just next to our visitor centre.

BBQs are a fire risk, endangering other people and the precious wildlife and habitats here. They are not permitted on the reserve at any time.

We welcome dogs in the Visitor Hub and they can be exercised in our car park on a short lead.

There are water bowls on the cafe terrace and at the Visitor Hub entrance and dog-friendly snacks can be bought during cafe opening hours.

Minsmere is home to rare and precious wildlife that needs our protection. To help us to minimise disturbance to our sensitive wildlife, we ask you not to walk your dogs on our nature trails.

Following the recent Wildfire there are fewer dog-friendly walks available due to several path closures, please ask in the Visitor Hub on arrival for a copy of the dog walking map. These walks are based in different areas of the reserve, and you will be given driving directions to these locations from the Visitor Hub.

Dogs die in hot cars, please do not leave your dog in the car when visiting us.

Assistance dogs are welcome in all parts of the reserve.

We encourage visitors to cycle or walk to Minsmere and have bike racks outside the visitor centre. Forgotten your bike lock? You are welcome to push your bikes along our trails to explore.

Please do not cycle on the nature trails for the safety of our visitors and wildlife.

### Recent sightings at Minsmere

Check out which species we've seen at Minsmere this week!

All our nature trails are now open, however we ask that all visitors check in at the Visitor Hub first so that we can give guidance on what areas are open and what to avoid.

Please note that the National Trust's Dunwich Heath remains closed to visitors.

Sightings update: 12 November

- Four [European White-fronted Geese](https://www.rspb.org.uk/birds-and-wildlife/white-fronted-goose), ten [Pink-footed Geese](https://www.rspb.org.uk/birds-and-wildlife/pink-footed-goose) and ten [Egyptian Geese](https://www.rspb.org.uk/birds-and-wildlife/egyptian-goose) were among the [Greylag Geese](https://www.rspb.org.uk/birds-and-wildlife/greylag-goose) on the Scrape on 12 November.
- Large flocks of [Wigeon](https://www.rspb.org.uk/birds-and-wildlife/wigeon), [Gadwall](https://www.rspb.org.uk/birds-and-wildlife/gadwall), [Teal](https://www.rspb.org.uk/birds-and-wildlife/teal), [Mallard](https://www.rspb.org.uk/birds-and-wildlife/mallard), [Pintail](https://www.rspb.org.uk/birds-and-wildlife/pintail), [Shoveler](https://www.rspb.org.uk/birds-and-wildlife/shoveler) and [Shelduck](https://www.rspb.org.uk/birds-and-wildlife/shelduck) looking resplendent on the Scrape.
- It was a good day for waders on the Scrape on 12 November, with sightings including six [Avocets](https://www.rspb.org.uk/birds-and-wildlife/avocet), a couple of [Dunlins](https://www.rspb.org.uk/birds-and-wildlife/dunlin), six [Black-tailed Godwits](https://www.rspb.org.uk/birds-and-wildlife/black-tailed-godwit), a [Bar-tailed Godwit](https://www.rspb.org.uk/birds-and-wildlife/bar-tailed-godwit), a [Greenshank](https://www.rspb.org.uk/birds-and-wildlife/greenshank), [Redshank](https://www.rspb.org.uk/birds-and-wildlife/redshank), a [Ruff](https://www.rspb.org.uk/birds-and-wildlife/ruff), several [Curlews](https://www.rspb.org.uk/birds-and-wildlife/curlew), [Turnstones](https://www.rspb.org.uk/birds-and-wildlife/turnstone) and [Snipe](https://www.rspb.org.uk/birds-and-wildlife/snipe) plus the regular [Lapwings](https://www.rspb.org.uk/birds-and-wildlife/lapwing).
- Both Caspian and [Yellow-legged Gulls](https://www.rspb.org.uk/birds-and-wildlife/yellow-legged-gull) were on the Scrape on 10-12 November.
- Five [Common Cranes](https://www.rspb.org.uk/birds-and-wildlife/crane) on the South Levels on 12 November.
- [Great Egrets](https://www.rspb.org.uk/birds-and-wildlife/great-white-egret) and [Grey Herons](https://www.rspb.org.uk/birds-and-wildlife/grey-heron) around the reedbed plus regular [Bitterns](https://www.rspb.org.uk/birds-and-wildlife/bittern) and [Little Egrets](https://www.rspb.org.uk/birds-and-wildlife/little-egret).
- [Kingfishers](https://www.rspb.org.uk/birds-and-wildlife/kingfisher) seen at Bittern Hide, Island Mere and around the Scrape.
- Up to three [Water Pipits](https://www.rspb.org.uk/birds-and-wildlife/water-pipit) remain among the [Meadow Pipits](https://www.rspb.org.uk/birds-and-wildlife/meadow-pipit) and [Pied Wagtails](https://www.rspb.org.uk/birds-and-wildlife/pied-wagtail) on the Scrape.
- [Bearded Tits](https://www.rspb.org.uk/birds-and-wildlife/bearded-tit) regular, especially at Island Mere, along North Wall and around South Hide.
- [Bullfinches](https://www.rspb.org.uk/birds-and-wildlife/bullfinch) and tit flocks regular in North Bushes, often with [Goldcrest](https://www.rspb.org.uk/birds-and-wildlife/goldcrest) and [Treecreeper](https://www.rspb.org.uk/birds-and-wildlife/treecreeper).
- A [Firecrest](https://www.rspb.org.uk/birds-and-wildlife/firecrest) near West Hide on 12 November.
- A large passage of [Fieldfares](https://www.rspb.org.uk/birds-and-wildlife/fieldfare) with a few [Redwings](https://www.rspb.org.uk/birds-and-wildlife/redwing) and [Song Thrushes](https://www.rspb.org.uk/birds-and-wildlife/song-thrush) this week.
- [Siskins](https://www.rspb.org.uk/birds-and-wildlife/siskin) regularly seen around the pond.
- Otters have been regular at Island Mere this week.
- Seawatching on 12 November produced sightings of [Common Scoters](https://www.rspb.org.uk/birds-and-wildlife/common-scoter), [Great Crested Grebes](https://www.rspb.org.uk/birds-and-wildlife/great-crested-grebe) and very rare Minsmere record of a [Red-necked Grebe](https://www.rspb.org.uk/birds-and-wildlife/red-necked-grebe).

### Group Bookings information

We ask that all groups (10 or more people) and externally led tours per-book their visit to RSPB Minsmere; note that we only have parking for two coaches per day.

You can make your Group Booking with us by emailing us at [minsmere@rspb.org.uk](mailto:minsmere@rspb.org.uk) or phoning our Visitor Centre at [01728 648281](tel:01728 648281).
